## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ad6e705bc7e5cdb6b03ca40ed8279f2783574620`
Local-runs: probe — the head's pure entry parser and matcher (`auth-manager.ts` lines 492-523 and 1170-1320, extracted verbatim by line into a scratch file outside the repository, blob `e3693b0b82`) run under node 22 against 48 corner inputs the pins do not name; every reading held
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts (`resolveClientAddress`, `firstHeader`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts (the by-name export list), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (`setMany`, `refuseByWritePredicates`, `validatePatch`, `firstPatternMiss`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts (`SettingsWritePredicateInput`, `SettingsWriteRefusal`, `SettingsValidationError`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts (the `SettingsValidationError` mapping), packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts (`allowed_ip_ranges`), packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts and sys-platform-setting.object.ts (`apiMethods`), docs/adr/0069-authentication-settings.md (D5). Prose faces (.changeset/allowed-ip-range-entry-rule.md, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx, docs/HARDENING.md) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; their sentences were read against the code here because the changeset and the guide state the same rule the module headers state.

Face: the paths decide no face (no published schema, no governed register row; `docs/HARDENING.md` is not `docs/adr/**`); the committed changeset's line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the closed-pair spelling, so the face is narrowing and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④ (`record-recognisers --paths` answers exactly this: no path face, the changeset's `Clause-②:` line decides). Rule under review: an `auth.allowed_ip_ranges` entry has one reading, shared by every door that judges or saves the list — an address, or an address, `/` and a prefix length in decimal digits within its family — and an entry that names no range is refused where it is saved or declared and matches no address at the gate. Full review (no prior at-tier record on any head; no `Contract-review-claim:` or hold on the PR; no review or comment on the PR at review time).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set narrowed, correctly stated.** `parseIpRange` (`auth-manager.ts` 1243-1259) is the one reading: `typeof` string, trimmed, no blank inside, base read by `readMatchedAddress` (IPv4 dotted-quad; IPv6 literal lowercased, zone identifier dropped, IPv4-mapped form folded to its IPv4 address), then either no `/`, or a prefix matching `^[0-9]{1,2}$` (IPv4 base) / `^[0-9]{1,3}$` (IPv6 base) read with `parseInt(…, 10)` and held to the width. The first `/` splits, so a second `/` lands in the prefix and is refused; ASCII digits only; `$` is end-of-string in JavaScript. Every other value reads `null`. Held, and the body's statement of the rule matches the code. Correct.
2. **Every caller of the parser, enumerated independently (`git grep` on the head tree, non-test sources).** `ipMatchesRange` is the only consumer of `parseIpRange` for a match, and its callers are: (a) the sign-in gate, `AuthManager.isClientIpAllowed` (6103-6107), called from the `${basePath}/*` middleware at `auth-plugin.ts` 3296 with the address `resolveClientAddress` established; (b) the settings save predicate, `allowedIpRangesWritePredicate` (`allowed-ip-ranges.ts` 203-230), on the address leg; (c) the plain-HTTP private/loopback host list, `isPrivateOrLoopbackHostLiteral` (`auth-manager.ts` 553-560), which passes five constant CIDRs and only after `ipv4ToInt(bare) !== null`; (d) `isLoopbackIssuer` (`auth-plugin.ts` 408-417), one constant `127.0.0.0/8` against a WHATWG-canonical hostname. `unreadableIpRangeEntries` is called by the save predicate, by `assertAllowedIpRanges`, and by the binding's `reportUnreadableAllowListEntries`. (c) and (d) pass well-formed constants and an address or hostname, so their verdicts are unchanged (probed: `127.0.0.2` in, `localhost` out, as before). No other caller exists. Correct.
3. **Every door that saves or reads the list, enumerated independently.** Writes: `PUT /api/settings/auth` → `setMany`; in-process `SettingsService.set` → `setMany` (2535); `setMany` → `validatePatch` → `refuseByWritePredicates` (2655), which asks the registered predicate on every write that changes the key, HTTP or not, and throws before any row is written; the predicate now judges the entries before `if (!transport)`, so the in-process leg reaches the entry refusal. `sys_setting` and `sys_platform_setting` carry `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`, so the data API opens no second write door. `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES` is read by the settings service as a locked env source, never written. Reads: `bindAuthSettings` (`auth-plugin.ts` 2403-2411) applies the stored or env list through `parseAllowedIpRanges` and now reports its unreadable entries; the declared list (plugin options, or an `auth:configure` handler — `ctx.trigger('auth:configure', authConfig)` at 764 precedes `new AuthManager(authConfig)` at 809) reaches `assertAllowedIpRanges` in the constructor (1784). `AuthManager` is constructed nowhere else in non-test source (a test-support helper and a script fixture aside). Covered: every door the rule names. Correct.
4. **No well-formed entry changed meaning.** Probed and pinned: IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR, `/32`, `/128`, bare addresses, `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` (each admitting its own family only, an IPv4-mapped client reading as IPv4 and so admitted by an IPv4 range, not by `::/0` — as before), leading zeros inside the digit count read decimal, bits past the prefix not judged, an IPv4-mapped base (dotted or hex) taking an IPv4 prefix, a zone identifier on either side dropped, surrounding blanks and CRLF trimmed, upper-case hex folded. Dotted-quad octets with leading zeros still read decimal (unchanged, both sides, the client side never carries them). What changed meaning is exactly the set the changeset's BREAKING banner names: an entry whose prefix is not decimal digits within its family, or whose text is not an address, now admits nobody. That is the narrowing, declared. Correct.
5. **The forwarded-address path can no longer produce a non-address match.** With `trustProxy` on, `resolveClientAddress` hands the gate the first comma-separated hop of the first forwarded header present (`client-address.ts` 61-90), unvalidated. The matcher now requires `readMatchedAddress(ip)` to read an address AND `parseIpRange(range)` to read a range before any comparison, and the only comparison left is the family's prefix comparison (`ipMatchesRange` 1308-1320). So a forwarded value that is not an address matches no entry under any list, and an entry that is not an address matches no client, its own spelling included (pinned at the unit level for both; probed for bracketed, blank-padded, empty and non-string clients). An undetermined address stays refused by `isClientIpAllowed` before the matcher. Correct, and fail-closed.
6. **IPv6 and IPv4-mapped corners.** `parseIpv6Literal` (492-523) accepts only `[0-9a-f:.]`, one `::`, 1-4 hex digits per group, an embedded dotted-quad only in the last position, exactly eight groups after elision; `readMatchedAddress` lowercases and drops the zone first, so `2001:DB8::/32` and `fe80::%eth0/10` read, while `fe80::/10%eth0` (zone after the prefix) and a bracketed literal do not. An IPv4-mapped base, dotted or hex, is an IPv4 address and takes an IPv4 prefix; an IPv6-sized prefix on it is refused (pinned, probed). `::ffff:0.0.0.0/0` is a well-formed `0.0.0.0/0`. Correct and consistent with the rule as the body states it.
7. **Fail-closed at bind.** A stored or env-pinned list holding an unreadable entry is applied with the entry in it; the entry matches nothing, so the gate admits only what the other entries admit, and a list of only such entries admits nobody (recovery is the env override, named in the log line and the guide). The alternative — refusing the patch at `applyConfigPatch` — would keep the standing (declared or empty) list in force, which can admit more than the stored one, so the dev's choice is the closed side. `reportUnreadableAllowListEntries` (3139-3159) logs once per distinct list at `error` with consequence and fix on the first line: the right level under the degradation rule, since the console shows the list as in force. The declared list is refused at construction (boot refuses), the loud side for a deployment's own code. Correct.
8. **Envelope.** The predicate returns `{ message, constraint: { invalidEntries } }`; `refuseByWritePredicates` wraps it as `FieldError` `{ field: 'allowed_ip_ranges', code: 'invalid_value', message, label, constraint }` (2905-2915) and throws `SettingsValidationError` (`code: 'SETTINGS_VALIDATION'`, `fields`); the route maps it to `400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION` with `details.fields` (`settings-routes.ts` 390-400). No new code, no new field-error member (ADR-0112, ADR-0114); `invalid_value` is the member the service already uses for every predicate refusal; `constraint` is a declared `Record<string, unknown>`. `AllowedIpRangesWriteRefusal.constraint` becomes a union — `allowed-ip-ranges.ts` is not re-exported from the package entry, so no published type moves. Correct.
9. **Refusal pins, code and status (ADR-0112).** Console save, first case (`allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` 398-412): `status` 400, `error.code` `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, field `code` `invalid_value`, `constraint`, message, nothing stored — complete. In-process case (423-431): `err.code` and `fields[0]` (`field`, `code`, `constraint`), nothing stored — complete for a door that has no HTTP status. Ordering case (414-421): `status` 400 and `fields[0].constraint`, **no `error.code` assertion** — the checklist requires both on every refusal case; the unique `constraint` shape does discriminate the refusal, but the code is the envelope's discriminator and is owed. **must-fix, see ④.** The construction refusal is a thrown `Error` matched on its text, the shape of its sibling `assertTrustedAppSchemes`; the gate pins are boolean on `isClientIpAllowed`, the `403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED` envelope being pinned on `main` already. Otherwise correct.
10. **Tests are rule tests and the ablation reads.** Unit: 24 unreadable entries across both families against the base, an inside and an outside client, a mapped client; four text entries; the well-formed control table; the gate through a mixed list; the constructor on a bad entry, a non-string, and a good list. Pin file: a new top-level `describe` in the existing harness (real `AuthPlugin`, real `SettingsService` with the shipped manifest, real settings routes), covering both save doors, the declared list, a pre-existing stored list, the env list, and preservation. Body: tests committed first and red on the merge base (`11 failed | 21 passed`, named to `da71a1fb9a` over source `b3d2f4bdb7`); six ablation legs on committed files, each red on the pins it should red and restored to a clean tree; package suite `4055 passed | 10 skipped`; typecheck exit 0, ledger unchanged. Readings are the dev's, named to this head; read-only here apart from the one probe on the Local-runs line.
11. **Public surface.** `ipMatchesRange` keeps its name and signature (a `typeof ip` guard added); `parseIpRange`, `unreadableIpRangeEntries`, `assertAllowedIpRanges`, `IpRange` are module exports not in the by-name list `index.ts` publishes from `auth-manager.ts` (lines 16-35), and `allowed-ip-ranges.ts` is not exported at all. No widening; `no (narrowing)` is the right arm. Correct.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/allowed-ip-range-entry-rule.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, title with `!`, a BREAKING banner naming who moves and the fix, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key changes; the setting's value domain is a runtime rule, not a spec key — no `allowedIpRanges` in `packages/spec/src`), exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate lists, with a reason that holds (no stored row is rewritten; a bad row is refused or inert). AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and disposition. The PR body carries the same declaration lines at line start, and `Skills-docs: updated here — …; skills/** teaches no allowed_ip_ranges` is present in both and holds (0 hits under `skills/` on the head tree). Touched packages: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (published, changeset present); `service-settings` and `platform-objects` are read, not changed. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no other login to name. Draft, base `main`, head repo equals base repo, `auto_merge` null, no governed path in the file list (register read at `GOVERNED_SURFACES`), no closing keyword in the body (a security-seat PR with no card).
- **CI at head `ad6e705bc7`: NOT MEASURED** — at review time the head carries 0 workflow runs and five queued check-suites (the head was pushed at 21:39Z and the PR reads `mergeable_state: dirty`, the dev merging `main`). Nothing here reads as green; the landing head owes all checks green and, for a `(narrowing)` PR, a `dogfood_battery` reading pinned to it — the body itself records the battery as NOT MEASURED and running.
- PR body: rule-level. It states the entry rule, the four doors, the kept readings and the envelope; it names no former behaviour beyond the replaced IPv6 exact-base case already public in `main`'s test name and docblock. Test names state the rule; the test data are the rule's boundary inputs. Commit titles and the changeset are rule-level. No leakage beyond the rule found.
- Acceptance notes, each answered: `/0` kept, own family only — held; bits past the prefix not refused — held and pinned; leading zeros within the digit count decimal — held; mapped base takes an IPv4 prefix — held; `applyConfigPatch` does not refuse, the binding reports — held, and the closed side (① item 7); save doors enumerated — held (① item 3); other callers pass constants — held (① item 2); nothing new on the package entry — held (① item 11); `test:repo` not run locally — CI's business.
- Prose faces, read against the code (for the lane seat): the guide's new rule paragraph and the amended "no address is checked for them" sentence hold; the `allowed_ip_ranges` row and the hardening row now say IPv4 or IPv6, which `ipv6PrefixEqual` already delivered on `main`. The changeset's "Saving the list already in force again is not judged, as before" holds (`refuseByWritePredicates` skips an unchanged key).
- Should (not blocking): the settings door's reading of a value that is not text is outside this rule and predates it; recorded for the seat in the local note, not here. Should: `applyConfigPatch` called by a host with an unreadable entry applies it closed with no line of its own (the binding is the only reporter) — a sentence on the method's docblock, or the report moved beside the patch, would keep "absence must be loud" at that door too. Should (docs-only, Tier H): ADR-0069 D5's note could record the entry rule. Nit: the manifest help text and its four translations describe the field without the prefix rule; the refusal message carries it.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face the narrowing is judged against what `main` declares. ADR-0069 D5 declares the allow-list as CIDR ranges judged by a gate before better-auth, and ADR-0049's hard constraint that a setting ships with the code path that enforces it; the `main` matcher's own docblock declared "an IPv4 CIDR, an IPv6 CIDR, or one exact address" and the manifest's help text "CIDR ranges or exact IPs". The diff takes nothing away from that declaration: every entry the declaration describes keeps its reading (① item 4, probed), and what it removes are readings the declaration never promised. The design is one parser at the one module every door already imported (`ipMatchesRange` was already "one matcher for every door"), so a list cannot be saved under one rule and enforced under another; refusal where a human or a deployment writes the list (save, declaration), inert-and-loud where nobody can be answered (a stored or env list at bind), and the closed side chosen at the one door where a refusal would have widened (`applyConfigPatch`). The envelope reuses the service's own predicate shape and an ADR-0114 member, and the entries are judged before the address so the entry refusal is reached whatever address the save comes from. The tests reach every door through the real plugin, service and routes, and the pure parser was probed here on the corners the pins do not name. The design holds.

One must-fix, in a file under review:

- **must-fix** — `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` lines 414-421 (the case "the console save names the unreadable entry first, whatever address it is saved from"): a refusal case asserts both `status` and `code` (ADR-0112 envelope; review checklist); this one asserts `status` and `constraint` only. Add the `error.code` (`SETTINGS_VALIDATION`) and the field `code` (`invalid_value`) assertions the first case on the same door already makes. No code change is owed.

Not blocking, recorded for the seat and the lane: the shoulds and the nit in ③; the CI and dogfood readings owed at the landing head; the delta hop covers the merge of `main` the PR is taking.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-r8`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgVfjk2i8T2D4RmxsKg`

Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts (`resolveClientAddress`, `firstHeader`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts (the by-name export list) and packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json (`exports`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-settings-declared.ts (`DECLARED_FIELDS`, `AUTH_SETTING_RESTORE`, `copyDeclared`, `captureDeclaredAuthOptions`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/settings-copy-locale.ts and settings-copy-locale.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts (`PLATFORM_LOCALES`), packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts (`setMany`, `validatePatch`, `refuseByWritePredicates`, `effectiveEnvOverride`, `coerceEnvValue`), packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts (`allowed_ip_ranges`), docs/adr/0069-enterprise-authentication-hardening.md (D5), scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs (`GOVERNED_SURFACES`). Face: `record-recognisers --paths` on the eight changed paths answers that the paths decide no face (no published schema, no governed register row: `docs/HARDENING.md` is prose, matching neither `docs/adr/**` nor `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, the register's only `docs/` rows) and defers to the committed changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries `no (narrowing)`, so the face is narrowing, the tier `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④, and the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces.
